newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates up on bank borrowings.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates up on bank borrowings.

text.p: *Volume expands to 34.944 bln pesos from 30.558 bln
Philippine interbank call loan rates rose to an average of 11.21875 percent on Tuesday from 11.125 due to heavy borrowing by government banks, traders said.
Done rates moved from 11.75 to 10.8125 percent, with 34 lenders and 26 borrowers.
"I believe government banks were window-dressing to balloon their books," a foreign bank trader said.
Dealers pointed out government banks were borrowing more than their usual requirements even for the Christmas holiday.
A dealer said the Central Bank may have been using them to siphon some money from the system.
Most of the banks, however, had already been well-positioned for any withdrawals due to Christmas spending, dealers said.
"What banks are most worried about is the six-day covering in the coming week," a big bank dealer said, referring to positions from Friday to Wednesday due to the New Year holidays.
Rates could shoot up if government banks keep on borrowing heavily, the dealer predicted.
